title: Loan Against SIP: Yes, and Your SIP Keeps Running

# Loan against SIP: how to borrow against your SIP and keep investing


*By Ashutosh Purohit*


Say you've run a SIP for a few years and now need money for a few months, but you don't want to stop the SIP or sell what it has built. You can take a loan against your SIP. You pledge the mutual fund units your SIP has already bought, they stay invested in your name, and your monthly SIP keeps running as before.


Strictly speaking, a SIP is just an instruction to invest a fixed amount every month. What you borrow against is the pile of units those instalments have bought. That's why a "loan against SIP" is the same thing as a loan against mutual funds, and it works the same way.


**The short version**


- You pledge the units your SIP has bought, and nothing is sold.
- Your SIP doesn't stop. It keeps buying units every month.
- You get a credit line and pay interest only on the amount you withdraw.
- At Yenmo, rates run from 9.89% to 10.49% a year, with no annual fee and no foreclosure charge.


## Can you take a loan against your SIP investment?


Yes, as long as the units are in a fund the lender accepts. Most equity, hybrid and debt funds qualify, whether you hold them as SOA with CAMS or KFintech or in a demat account through a broker. If you're not sure which form yours are in, our guide to[demat vs SOA mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/blog/demat-vs-soa-mutual-funds) explains how to check.


The main exception is ELSS. Every ELSS instalment is locked in for 3 years from the day it's invested, and only units past that lock-in can be pledged. So if your ELSS SIP has run for four years, roughly the first year's instalments can be pledged today, and the rest become eligible month by month.


## What happens to your SIP after you pledge?


Nothing changes. Your SIP keeps running on the same date from the same bank account, and the new units it buys are yours to hold or pledge.


The pledge is a lien, which is a hold that stops the pledged units from being sold or redeemed while the loan is open. For funds held with CAMS or KFintech, the lien is marked with the registrar. The units never move to Yenmo or to the lender, and they keep earning whatever the fund earns.


Your limit is worked out from the units you pledge. As your SIP adds units, you can pledge more of them later to raise what you can withdraw, without signing a new agreement.


## How much can you borrow against your SIP?


It depends on what kind of fund your SIP invests in. The lender lends a fixed share of the fund's value, called the loan-to-value or LTV.


Fund type LTV through Yenmo (Bajaj Finance)


Equity funds 50%


Liquid funds Up to 90%


Other debt funds Typically 70%–80%


The 50% on equity funds is an RBI limit for NBFC lenders, set in the[NBFC Credit Facilities Directions, 2025](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12957#C8C) . Debt funds move less in price, so lenders allow more against them.


The smallest loan at Yenmo is ₹25,000, so you'd need about ₹50,000 in equity funds, or less if your SIP is in debt funds. Once your line is open, you can withdraw as little as ₹500 at a time. You can try your own numbers on the[loan against mutual fund calculator](https://yenmo.in/calculators/loan-against-mutual-fund-calculator) .


## What it costs: a worked example


Say Priya has put ₹15,000 a month into two equity index funds for a little over three years, and the units are now worth ₹6 lakh. She needs ₹1.5 lakh for a family wedding and expects her bonus to cover it in four months.


At 50% LTV, her ₹6 lakh of funds lets her withdraw up to ₹3 lakh. Because her SIP will keep adding to the portfolio, she asks for a sanctioned limit of ₹4 lakh. That leaves room to pledge new units later without a new agreement or a second processing fee. Until she does, she can still withdraw only up to ₹3 lakh.


A ₹4 lakh sanction falls in the ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh slab, so her rate is 10.39% a year. She withdraws ₹1.5 lakh and pays interest only on that:


- ₹1,50,000 × 10.39% = ₹15,585 a year, or about ₹1,300 a month
- Over four months, that's about ₹5,200 in interest
- She also pays a one-time processing fee of ₹1,649 + GST


When the bonus arrives, she repays the full amount with no foreclosure charge. Her SIP never missed a month, and every unit she owned is still invested.


If she had sold ₹1.5 lakh of units instead, those units would stop growing for good. She could also owe tax on the gain: 20% on equity units held 12 months or less, or 12.5% on long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year.

No loan at Yenmo is priced over 10.49% a year. Loans are given by our lending partner Bajaj Finance as a 3-year credit line, with no EMI.


You pay interest each month on what you've withdrawn and repay the amount itself whenever you like. There's no annual fee during the three years and no charge for paying back early. Smaller charges, such as pledge and unpledge fees, are listed on our[charges page](https://yenmo.in/charges) .


## What should you watch out for?


The biggest risk is a market fall. Your limit is tied to the current value of your pledged units, so if markets drop, your limit drops too. Bajaj Finance compares that limit with the amount you've actually withdrawn. If the limit falls to 90% of what you've withdrawn, you have 7 business days to repay part of it or pledge more units. If it falls below 85%, Bajaj can sell pledged units straight away, after informing you.


What protects you is borrowing well within your limit. Priya withdrew ₹1.5 lakh against a ₹3 lakh limit, so her funds would have to fall by 55%, from ₹6 lakh to ₹2.7 lakh, before she was asked to top up. Had she withdrawn the full ₹3 lakh, a 10% fall would have been enough.


A loan also makes most sense for a short or known need. If you'd need years to repay, add up the interest and compare it with what your funds are likely to earn before you borrow.


## How do you get a loan against your SIP at Yenmo?


Start with the eligibility check on the[loan against mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/products/loan-against-mutual-funds) page. It begins with the mobile number linked to your investments. You'll need your PAN, Aadhaar for KYC and a bank account, and there's no minimum credit score.


For funds held with CAMS or KFintech, the whole application takes about 5 to 7 minutes online. For funds in a demat account, you start by writing tosupport@yenmo.in , and the rest is digital with no forms.


One account can take SIP units from several places at once, such as CAMS folios and a Zerodha or Groww demat. Here's[how pledging across brokers works](https://yenmo.in/blog/pledge-mutual-funds-across-zerodha-groww-other-brokers) . When you've repaid, you unpledge from the Yenmo app or website by picking the fund and units and pressing a button.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I take a loan against my SIP?


Yes. You pledge the mutual fund units your SIP has bought and get a credit line against them, while the units stay invested in your name. At Yenmo, loans start at ₹25,000, through Bajaj Finance.


### Does my SIP stop if I pledge my mutual funds?


No. Your SIP continues after you pledge, on the same date and from the same bank account. Only the units you choose to pledge are held under a lien.


### How much loan can I get against my SIP?


It depends on the fund type. Through Yenmo, you can borrow 50% of the value of equity funds, up to 90% of liquid funds and typically 70% to 80% of other debt funds.


### What is the interest rate on a loan against SIP?


At Yenmo, rates run from 9.89% to 10.49% a year, depending on your sanctioned limit, and no loan is priced over 10.49%. You pay interest only on the amount you withdraw, not on the whole limit.


### Can I add new SIP units to my loan later?


Yes. You can pledge more units at any time to raise what you can withdraw, up to your sanctioned limit. This needs no new agreement and no new processing fee, though pledge charges apply as shown on the charges page.


### Can I pledge ELSS units bought through a SIP?


Yes, once they finish their lock-in. Each ELSS instalment is locked in for 3 years from the day it was invested, so with an ELSS SIP your older instalments become eligible first, one month at a time.
